1.92.m: and the one named Madhyameśvara, as well as Pāśupateśvara, / Śaṅkukarṇeśvara, and both the Gokarṇas,

1.92.s:
drumacaṇḍeśvaraṃ nāma bhadreśvaram anuttamam
sthāneśvaraṃ tathaikāgraṃ kāleśvaram ajeśvaram //
1.92.d:
द्रुमचण्डेश्वरं नाम भद्रेश्वरम् अनुत्तमम्
स्थानेश्वरं तथैकाग्रं कालेश्वरम् अजेश्वरम् ॥
1.92.m: the one named Drumacaṇḍeśvara, the unsurpassed Bhadreśvara, / Sthāneśvara, likewise the one-pointed Kāleśvara, Ajeśvara,

1.92.s:
bhairaveśvaram īśānaṃ tathauṃkārakasaṃjñitam
amareśaṃ mahākālaṃ jyotiṣaṃ bhasmagātrakam //
1.92.d:
भैरवेश्वरम् ईशानं तथौंकारकसंज्ञितम्
अमरेशं महाकालं ज्योतिषं भस्मगात्रकम् ॥
1.92.m: Bhairaveśvara, Īśāna, and the one named Oṃkāraka, / Amareśa, Mahākāla, Jyotiṣa, and Bhasmagātraka,

1.92.s:
yāni cānyāni puṇyāni sthānāni mama bhūtale
aṣṭaṣaṣṭisamākhyāni rūḍhānyanyāni kṛtsnaśaḥ //
1.92.d:
यानि चान्यानि पुण्यानि स्थानानि मम भूतले
अष्टषष्टिसमाख्यानि रूढान्यन्यानि कृत्स्नशः ॥
1.92.m: and whatever other sacred places of mine there are on the earth's surface, / sixty-eight in number, well-established and all others in their entirety,

1.92.s:
tāni sarvāṇyaśeṣāṇi vārāṇasyāṃ viśanti mām
sarvaparvasu puṇyeṣu guhyaṃ caitadudāhṛtam //
1.92.d:
तानि सर्वाण्यशेषाणि वाराणस्यां विशन्ति माम्
सर्वपर्वसु पुण्येषु गुह्यं चैतदुदाहृतम् ॥
1.92.m: all of them without exception enter into me in Vārāṇasī / on all auspicious festive days; and this has been declared as a secret.

1.92.s:
teneha labhate jantur mṛto divyāmṛtaṃ padam
snātasya caiva gaṅgāyāṃ dṛṣṭena ca mayā śubhe //
1.92.d:
तेनेह लभते जन्तुर् मृतो दिव्यामृतं पदम्
स्नातस्य चैव गङ्गायां दृष्टेन च मया शुभे ॥
1.92.m: Therefore a creature who dies here attains the divine immortal abode; / and for one who has bathed in the Gaṅgā and seen me, O auspicious one,

1.92.s:
sarvayajñaphalaistulyam iṣṭaiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
sadya eva samāpnoti kiṃ tataḥ paramādbhutam //
1.92.d:
सर्वयज्ञफलैस्तुल्यम् इष्टैः शतसहस्रशः
सद्य एव समाप्नोति किं ततः परमाद्भुतम् ॥
1.92.m: he instantly attains the fruit equal to all sacrifices / offered by hundreds of thousands. What could be more wondrous than that?

1.92.s:
sarvāyatanamukhyāni divi bhūmau giriṣv api
parātparataraṃ devī budhyasveti mayoditam //
1.92.d:
सर्वायतनमुख्यानि दिवि भूमौ गिरिष्व् अपि
परात्परतरं देवी बुध्यस्वेति मयोदितम् ॥
1.92.m: The foremost of all shrines in heaven, on earth, and also in the mountains, / know it, O goddess, to be higher than the highest, as told by me.

1.92.s:
aviśabdena pāpastu vedoktaḥ kathyate dvijaiḥ
tena muktaṃ mayā juṣṭam avimuktam ata ucyate //
1.92.d:
अविशब्देन पापस्तु वेदोक्तः कथ्यते द्विजैः
तेन मुक्तं मया जुष्टम् अविमुक्तम् अत उच्यते ॥
1.92.m: By the word 'avi', sin spoken of in the Vedas is meant by the twice-born; / freed from that, it is inhabited by me, hence it is called Avimukta.”

1.92.s:
ityuktvā bhagavān rudraḥ sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ
sudṛṣṭaṃ kuru deveśi avimuktaṃ gṛhaṃ mama //
1.92.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् रुद्रः सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः
सुदृष्टं कुरु देवेशि अविमुक्तं गृहं मम ॥
1.92.m: Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord Rudra, the Maheśvara of all the worlds, [said:] / “Behold well, O ruler of gods, Avimukta, my home.”

1.92.s:
ityuktvā bhagavān devas tayā sārdham umāpatiḥ
darśayāmāsa bhagavān śrīparvatamanuttamam //
1.92.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् देवस् तया सार्धम् उमापतिः
दर्शयामास भगवान् श्रीपर्वतमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.92.m: Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord, the god, the lord of Umā, / together with her showed her the unsurpassed Śrīparvata.

1.92.s:
avimukteśvare nityam avasacca sadā tayā
sarvagatvācca sarvatvāt sarvātmā sadasanmayaḥ //
1.92.d:
अविमुक्तेश्वरे नित्यम् अवसच्च सदा तया
सर्वगत्वाच्च सर्वत्वात् सर्वात्मा सदसन्मयः ॥
1.92.m: He constantly resided at Avimukteśvara, ever with her; / and because he is all-pervading and omnipresent, the Self of all consists of both being and non-being.

1.92.s:
śrīparvatamanuprāpya devyā deveśvaro haraḥ
kṣetrāṇi darśayāmāsa sarvabhūtapatirbhavaḥ //
1.92.d:
श्रीपर्वतमनुप्राप्य देव्या देवेश्वरो हरः
क्षेत्राणि दर्शयामास सर्वभूतपतिर्भवः ॥
1.92.m: Reaching Śrīparvata with the goddess, Hara, the lord of gods, / Bhava, the lord of all beings, showed her the sacred fields:

1.92.s:
kuṇḍīprabhaṃ ca paramaṃ divyaṃ vaiśravaṇeśvaram
āśāliṅgaṃ ca deveśaṃ divyaṃ yacca bileśvaram //
1.92.d:
कुण्डीप्रभं च परमं दिव्यं वैश्रवणेश्वरम्
आशालिङ्गं च देवेशं दिव्यं यच्च बिलेश्वरम् ॥
1.92.m: The supreme Kuṇḍīprabha, divine Vaiśravaṇeśvara, / the lord of gods Āśāliṅga, and divine Bileśvara,

1.92.s:
rāmeśvaraṃ ca paramaṃ viṣṇunā yatpratiṣṭhitam
dakṣiṇadvārapārśve tu kuṇḍaleśvaramīśvaram //
1.92.d:
रामेश्वरं च परमं विष्णुना यत्प्रतिष्ठितम्
दक्षिणद्वारपार्श्वे तु कुण्डलेश्वरमीश्वरम् ॥
1.92.m: the supreme Rāmeśvara, which was installed by Viṣṇu, / and beside the southern gate, Lord Kuṇḍaleśvaram,

1.92.s:
pūrvadvārasamīpasthaṃ tripurāntakamuttamam
vivṛddhaṃ giriṇā sārdhaṃ devadevanamaskṛtam //
1.92.d:
पूर्वद्वारसमीपस्थं त्रिपुरान्तकमुत्तमम्
विवृद्धं गिरिणा सार्धं देवदेवनमस्कृतम् ॥
1.92.m: the excellent Tripurāntaka situated near the eastern gate, / which grew together with the mountain and is bowed to by the god of gods,

1.92.s:
madhyameśvaramityuktaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
amareśvaraṃ ca varadaṃ devaiḥ pūrvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam //
1.92.d:
मध्यमेश्वरमित्युक्तं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम्
अमरेश्वरं च वरदं देवैः पूर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
1.92.m: the one called Madhyameśvara, renowned in the three worlds, / and the boon-giving Amareśvara, installed formerly by the gods,

1.92.s:
gocarmeśvaram īśānaṃ tathendreśvaram adbhutam
karmeśvaraṃ ca vipulaṃ kāryārthaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam //
1.92.d:
गोचर्मेश्वरम् ईशानं तथेन्द्रेश्वरम् अद्भुतम्
कर्मेश्वरं च विपुलं कार्यार्थं ब्रह्मणा कृतम् ॥
1.92.m: Gocarmeśvara, Īśāna, and wondrous Indreśvara, / and the extensive Karmeśvara, made by Brahmā for the sake of his purpose,

1.92.s:
śrīmatsiddhavaṭaṃ caiva sadāvāso mamāvyaye
ajena nirmitaṃ divyaṃ sākṣādajabilaṃ śubham //
1.92.d:
श्रीमत्सिद्धवटं चैव सदावासो ममाव्यये
अजेन निर्मितं दिव्यं साक्षादजबिलं शुभम् ॥
1.92.m: the glorious Siddhavata, my perpetual dwelling, O imperishable one, / the auspicious, manifest Ajabila, fashioned divine by Aja,

1.92.s:
tatraiva pāduke divye madīye ca bileśvare
tatra śṛṅgāṭakākāraṃ śṛṅgāṭācalamadhyame //
1.92.d:
तत्रैव पादुके दिव्ये मदीये च बिलेश्वरे
तत्र शृङ्गाटकाकारं शृङ्गाटाचलमध्यमे ॥
1.92.m: right there my divine sandals in Bileśvara; / there, shaped like a four-way crossway, in the middle of Mount Śṛṅgāṭa,

1.92.s:
śṛṅgāṭakeśvaraṃ nāma śrīdevyā tu pratiṣṭhitam
mallikārjunakaṃ caiva mama vāsamidaṃ śubham //
1.92.d:
शृङ्गाटकेश्वरं नाम श्रीदेव्या तु प्रतिष्ठितम्
मल्लिकार्जुनकं चैव मम वासमिदं शुभम् ॥
1.92.m: the one named Śṛṅgāṭakeśvara, installed by the glorious goddess, / and Mallikārjunaka, this auspicious abode of mine,

1.92.s:
rajeśvaraṃ ca paryāye rajasā supratiṣṭhitam
gajeśvaraṃ ca vaiśākhaṃ kapoteśvaramavyayam //
1.92.d:
रजेश्वरं च पर्याये रजसा सुप्रतिष्ठितम्
गजेश्वरं च वैशाखं कपोतेश्वरमव्ययम् ॥
1.92.m: Rajeśvara, well installed in due succession with dust, / Gajeśvara, Vaiśākha, and imperishable Kapoteśvara,

1.92.s:
koṭīśvaraṃ mahātīrthaṃ rudrakoṭigaṇaiḥ purā
sevitaṃ devi paśyādya sarvasmādadhikaṃ śubham //
1.92.d:
कोटीश्वरं महातीर्थं रुद्रकोटिगणैः पुरा
सेवितं देवि पश्याद्य सर्वस्मादधिकं शुभम् ॥
1.92.m: Koṭīśvara, the great sacred ford, formerly frequented / by the hosts of crores of Rudras; see it today, O goddess, more auspicious than all.

1.92.s:
dvidevakulasaṃjñaṃ ca brahmaṇā dakṣiṇe śubham
uttare sthāpitaṃ caiva viṣṇunā caiva śailajam //
1.92.d:
द्विदेवकुलसंज्ञं च ब्रह्मणा दक्षिणे शुभम्
उत्तरे स्थापितं चैव विष्णुना चैव शैलजम् ॥
1.92.m: And the auspicious one called Dvidevakula on the south by Brahmā, / and established on the north by Viṣṇu, born of the mountain,

1.92.s:
mahāpramāṇaliṅgaṃ ca mayā pūrvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
paścime parvate paśya brahmeśvaramaleśvaram //
1.92.d:
महाप्रमाणलिङ्गं च मया पूर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्
पश्चिमे पर्वते पश्य ब्रह्मेश्वरमलेश्वरम् ॥
1.92.m: and the liṅga of great measure, formerly installed by me; / look upon Brahmeśvara and Aleśvara on the western mountain.

1.92.s:
alaṃkṛtaṃ tvayā brahman purastān munibhiḥ saha
ityuktvā tadgṛhe tiṣṭhad alaṃgṛhamiti smṛtam //
1.92.d:
अलंकृतं त्वया ब्रह्मन् पुरस्तान् मुनिभिः सह
इत्युक्त्वा तद्गृहे तिष्ठद् अलंगृहमिति स्मृतम् ॥
1.92.m: “It has been adorned by you, O Brahmā, in front together with the sages.” / Saying this, he stayed in that dwelling, which is commemorated as Alaṃgṛha.

1.92.s:
tatrāpi tīrthaṃ tīrthajñe vyomaliṅgaṃ ca paśya me
kadambeśvaram etaddhi skandenaiva pratiṣṭhitam //
1.92.d:
तत्रापि तीर्थं तीर्थज्ञे व्योमलिङ्गं च पश्य मे
कदम्बेश्वरम् एतद्धि स्कन्देनैव प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
1.92.m: There also is a sacred ford, O knower of sacred fords; behold my Vyomaliṅga. / This is Kadambeśvara, installed by Skanda himself,

1.92.s:
gomaṇḍaleśvaraṃ caiva nandādyaiḥ supratiṣṭhitam
devaiḥ sarvaistu śakrādyaiḥ sthāpitāni varānane //
1.92.d:
गोमण्डलेश्वरं चैव नन्दाद्यैः सुप्रतिष्ठितम्
देवैः सर्वैस्तु शक्राद्यैः स्थापितानि वरानने ॥
1.92.m: and Gomaṇḍaleśvara, well installed by Nandā and others; / all these were established by the gods headed by Śakra, O fair-faced one.

1.92.s:
śrīmaddevahradaprānte sthānānīmāni paśya me
tathā hārapure devi tava hāre nipātite //
1.92.d:
श्रीमद्देवह्रदप्रान्ते स्थानानीमानि पश्य मे
तथा हारपुरे देवि तव हारे निपातिते ॥
1.92.m: Behold these places of mine on the edge of the glorious Devahrada. / Likewise, O goddess, in Hārapura, when your necklace fell down,

1.92.s:
tvayā hitāya jagatāṃ hārakuṇḍamidaṃ kṛtam
śivarudrapure caiva tatkāyopari suvrate //
1.92.d:
त्वया हिताय जगतां हारकुण्डमिदं कृतम्
शिवरुद्रपुरे चैव तत्कायोपरि सुव्रते ॥
1.92.m: this Hārakuṇḍa was made by you for the welfare of the worlds; / and in Śivarudrapura, over that body, O lady of good vows,

1.92.s:
tatra pitrā suśailena sthāpitaṃ tvacaleśvaram
alaṃkṛtaṃ mayā brahma purastān munibhiḥ saha //
1.92.d:
तत्र पित्रा सुशैलेन स्थापितं त्वचलेश्वरम्
अलंकृतं मया ब्रह्म पुरस्तान् मुनिभिः सह ॥
1.92.m: there Acaleśvara was established by your father, the good mountain. / “O Brahmā, it was adorned by me in front along with the sages.”

1.92.s:
caṇḍikeśvarakaṃ devi caṇḍikeśā tavātmajā
caṇḍikānirmitaṃ sthānam aṃbikātīrtham uttamam //
1.92.d:
चण्डिकेश्वरकं देवि चण्डिकेशा तवात्मजा
चण्डिकानिर्मितं स्थानम् अंबिकातीर्थम् उत्तमम् ॥
1.92.m: Caṇḍikeśvaraka, O goddess, whose Caṇḍikā is your daughter, / the place fashioned by Caṇḍikā, the excellent sacred ford of Aṃbikā.

1.92.s:
rucikeśvarakaṃ caiva dhāraiṣā kapilā śubhā
eteṣu devi sthāneṣu tīrtheṣu vividheṣu ca //
1.92.d:
रुचिकेश्वरकं चैव धारैषा कपिला शुभा
एतेषु देवि स्थानेषु तीर्थेषु विविधेषु च ॥
1.92.m: And Rucikeśvaraka, and this auspicious stream Kapilā; / in these places and various sacred sites, O goddess,

1.92.s:
pūjayenmāṃ sadā bhaktyā mayā sārdhaṃ hi modate
śrīśaile saṃtyajed dehaṃ brāhmaṇo dagdhakilbiṣaḥ //
1.92.d:
पूजयेन्मां सदा भक्त्या मया सार्धं हि मोदते
श्रीशैले संत्यजेद् देहं ब्राह्मणो दग्धकिल्बिषः ॥
1.92.m: one should always worship me with devotion; he rejoices with me. / A brāhmaṇa whose sins are burned away who abandons his body at Śrīśaila,

1.92.s:
mucyate nātra saṃdeho hy avimukte yathā śubham
mahāsnānaṃ ca yaḥ kuryād ghṛtena vidhinaiva tu //
1.92.d:
मुच्यते नात्र संदेहो ह्य् अविमुक्ते यथा शुभम्
महास्नानं च यः कुर्याद् घृतेन विधिनैव तु ॥
1.92.m: is liberated—there is no doubt about this—just as auspiciously in Avimukta. / And whoever performs the great bath with ghee according to the rule,

1.92.s:
sa yāti mama sāyujyaṃ sthāneṣveteṣu suvrate
snānaṃ palaśataṃ jñeyam abhyaṅgaṃ pañcaviṃśati //
1.92.d:
स याति मम सायुज्यं स्थानेष्वेतेषु सुव्रते
स्नानं पलशतं ज्ञेयम् अभ्यङ्गं पञ्चविंशति ॥
1.92.m: he attains intimate union with me in these places, O lady of good vows. / A bath is known to be one hundred palas, an unction twenty-five [palas];

1.92.s:
palānāṃ dve sahasre tu mahāsnānaṃ prakīrtitam
snāpya liṅgaṃ madīyaṃ tu gavyenaiva ghṛtena ca //
1.92.d:
पलानां द्वे सहस्रे तु महास्नानं प्रकीर्तितम्
स्नाप्य लिङ्गं मदीयं तु गव्येनैव घृतेन च ॥
1.92.m: the great bath is proclaimed to be of two thousand palas. / Having bathed my liṅga with ghee produced from cow's milk,

1.92.s:
viśodhya sarvadravyaistu vāribhir abhiṣiñcati
saṃmārjya śatayajñānāṃ snānena prayutaṃ tathā //
1.92.d:
विशोध्य सर्वद्रव्यैस्तु वारिभिर् अभिषिञ्चति
संमार्ज्य शतयज्ञानां स्नानेन प्रयुतं तथा ॥
1.92.m: and purified it with all substances, he sprinkles it with waters. / Having wiped it, [the merit] of a hundred sacrifices is gained by a bath, and a million

1.92.s:
pūjayā śatasāhasram anantaṃ gītavādinām
mahāsnāne prasaktaṃ tu snānamaṣṭaguṇaṃ smṛtam //
1.92.d:
पूजया शतसाहस्रम् अनन्तं गीतवादिनाम्
महास्नाने प्रसक्तं तु स्नानमष्टगुणं स्मृतम् ॥
1.92.m: by worship, a hundred thousand [by music], and endless [merit] by singers and musicians. / When one is devoted to the great bath, the bath is considered eight times greater,

1.92.s:
jalena kevalenaiva gandhatoyena bhaktitaḥ
anulepanaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ pañcaviṃśatpalena vai //
1.92.d:
जलेन केवलेनैव गन्धतोयेन भक्तितः
अनुलेपनं तु तत् सर्वं पञ्चविंशत्पलेन वै ॥
1.92.m: with water alone or with fragrant water offered with devotion. / The unguent altogether should be twenty-five palas.

1.92.s:
śamīpuṣpaṃ ca vidhinā bilvapatraṃ ca paṅkajam
anyānyapi ca puṣpāṇi bilvapatraṃ na saṃtyajet //
1.92.d:
शमीपुष्पं च विधिना बिल्वपत्रं च पङ्कजम्
अन्यान्यपि च पुष्पाणि बिल्वपत्रं न संत्यजेत् ॥
1.92.m: Śamī flowers according to the rule, bilva leaves, and lotus, / and other flowers as well; one must not omit the bilva leaf.

1.92.s:
caturdroṇair mahādevam aṣṭadroṇairathāpi vā
daśadroṇais tu naivedyam aṣṭadroṇairathāpi vā //
1.92.d:
चतुर्द्रोणैर् महादेवम् अष्टद्रोणैरथापि वा
दशद्रोणैस् तु नैवेद्यम् अष्टद्रोणैरथापि वा ॥
1.92.m: To Mahādeva [one should offer a food offering] of four droṇas, or eight droṇas, / or a food offering of ten droṇas, or else of eight droṇas.

1.92.s:
śatadroṇasamaṃ puṇyam āḍhake 'pi vidhīyate
vittahīnasya viprasya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.92.d:
शतद्रोणसमं पुण्यम् आढके ऽपि विधीयते
वित्तहीनस्य विप्रस्य नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.92.m: Merit equal to a hundred droṇas is prescribed even for an āḍhaka / for a brāhmaṇa who lacks wealth; no doubt should be entertained here.

1.92.s:
bherīmṛdaṅgamurajatimirāpaṭahādibhiḥ
vāditrairvividhaiścānyair ninādairvividhairapi //
1.92.d:
भेरीमृदङ्गमुरजतिमिरापटहादिभिः
वादित्रैर्विविधैश्चान्यैर् निनादैर्विविधैरपि ॥
1.92.m: With kettle-drums, mṛdaṅgas, murajas, timirās, paṭahas, and the like, / with various musical instruments and other diverse sounds,

1.92.s:
jāgaraṃ kārayedyastu prārthayecca yathākramam
sa bhṛtyaputradāraiś ca tathā saṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
1.92.d:
जागरं कारयेद्यस्तु प्रार्थयेच्च यथाक्रमम्
स भृत्यपुत्रदारैश् च तथा संबन्धिबान्धवैः ॥
1.92.m: he who keeps vigil and prays in proper order, / he, together with servants, sons, wives, and relations and kinsmen,

1.92.s:
sārdhaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā prārthayelliṅgam uttamam
dravyahīnaṃ kriyāhīnaṃ śraddhāhīnaṃ sureśvara //
1.92.d:
सार्धं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा प्रार्थयेल्लिङ्गम् उत्तमम्
द्रव्यहीनं क्रियाहीनं श्रद्धाहीनं सुरेश्वर ॥
1.92.m: having made circumambulation, should pray to the supreme liṅga: / 'Lacking wealth, lacking rites, lacking faith, O Lord of gods,

1.92.s:
kṛtaṃ vā na kṛtaṃ vāpi kṣantumarhasi śaṅkara
ityuktvā vai japedrudraṃ tvaritaṃ śāntimeva ca //
1.92.d:
कृतं वा न कृतं वापि क्षन्तुमर्हसि शङ्कर
इत्युक्त्वा वै जपेद्रुद्रं त्वरितं शान्तिमेव च ॥
1.92.m: done or not done, you ought to forgive it, O Śaṅkara.' / Having spoken thus, he should quickly recite the Rudra hymn for peace.

1.92.s:
japitvaivaṃ mahābījaṃ tathā pañcākṣarasya vai
sa evaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvayajñeṣu yatphalam //
1.92.d:
जपित्वैवं महाबीजं तथा पञ्चाक्षरस्य वै
स एवं सर्वतीर्थेषु सर्वयज्ञेषु यत्फलम् ॥
1.92.m: Having thus recited the great seed-syllable and the five-syllable mantra, / whatever fruit is obtained in all sacred sites and in all sacrifices,

1.92.s:
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti vārāṇasyāṃ yathā mṛtaḥ
tathaiva mama sāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.92.d:
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति वाराणस्यां यथा मृतः
तथैव मम सायुज्यं लभते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.92.m: that fruit he fully obtains, just as one who dies in Vārāṇasī; / likewise he attains intimate union with me, there is no doubt about this.

1.92.s:
matpriyārthamidaṃ kāryaṃ madbhaktairvidhipūrvakam
ye na kurvanti te bhaktā na bhavanti na saṃśayaḥ //
1.92.d:
मत्प्रियार्थमिदं कार्यं मद्भक्तैर्विधिपूर्वकम्
ये न कुर्वन्ति ते भक्ता न भवन्ति न संशयः ॥
1.92.m: This is to be done according to the rule by my devotees for my pleasure; / those who do not do it are not devotees, there is no doubt."

1.92.s:
sūta uvāca
niśamya vacanaṃ devī gatvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm
avimukteśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ payasā ca ghṛtena ca //
1.92.d:
सूत उवाच
निशम्य वचनं देवी गत्वा वाराणसीं पुरीम्
अविमुक्तेश्वरं लिङ्गं पयसा च घृतेन च ॥
1.92.m: Sūta said: / Hearing his words, the goddess went to the city of Vārāṇasī, / and the Avimukteśvara liṅga, with milk and ghee,

1.92.s:
arcayāmāsa deveśaṃ rudraṃ bhuvananāyakam
avimukte ca tapasā mandarasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.92.d:
अर्चयामास देवेशं रुद्रं भुवननायकम्
अविमुक्ते च तपसा मन्दरस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.92.m: she worshipped, [honouring] the lord of gods, Rudra, ruler of the universe. / And through the austerity of the great-souled Mandara at Avimukta,

1.92.s:
kalpayāmāsa vai kṣetraṃ mandare cārukandare
tatrāndhakaṃ mahādaityaṃ hiraṇyākṣasutaṃ prabhuḥ //
1.92.d:
कल्पयामास वै क्षेत्रं मन्दरे चारुकन्दरे
तत्रान्धकं महादैत्यं हिरण्याक्षसुतं प्रभुः ॥
1.92.m: he prepared the sacred field in the beautiful cave of Mandara. / There, having shown grace to the great daitya Andhaka, son of Hiraṇyākṣa,

1.92.s:
anugṛhya gaṇatvaṃ ca prāpayāmāsa līlayā
etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ kathāsarvasvamādarāt //
1.92.d:
अनुगृह्य गणत्वं च प्रापयामास लीलया
एतद्वः कथितं सर्वं कथासर्वस्वमादरात् ॥
1.92.m: the Lord raised him playfully to the status of a gaṇa. / All this has been narrated to you with respect, the whole essence of the story.

1.92.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi kṣetramāhātmyamuttamam
sarvakṣetreṣu yatpuṇyaṃ tatsarvaṃ sahasā labhet //
1.92.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि क्षेत्रमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम्
सर्वक्षेत्रेषु यत्पुण्यं तत्सर्वं सहसा लभेत् ॥
1.92.m: Whoever reads or listens to this supreme majesty of the sacred field / quickly obtains all the merit that exists in all sacred fields.

1.92.s:
śrāvayedvā dvijānsarvān kṛtaśaucān jitendriyān
sa eva sarvayajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ //
1.92.d:
श्रावयेद्वा द्विजान्सर्वान् कृतशौचान् जितेन्द्रियान्
स एव सर्वयज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
1.92.m: Or if he recites it to all twice-born who are purified and have subdued their senses, / that man obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.

1.93.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
andhako nāma daityendro mandare cārukandare
damitastu kathaṃ lebhe gāṇapatyaṃ maheśvarāt //
1.93.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
अन्धको नाम दैत्येन्द्रो मन्दरे चारुकन्दरे
दमितस्तु कथं लेभे गाणपत्यं महेश्वरात् ॥
1.93.m: The sages said: / "How did the lord of daityas named Andhaka, in the beautiful cave of Mandara, / being subdued, obtain the status of gaṇa-lord from Maheśvara?

1.93.s:
vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ yathāśrutam
andhakānugrahaṃ caiva mandare śoṣaṇaṃ tathā //
1.93.d:
वक्तुमर्हसि चास्माकं यथावृत्तं यथाश्रुतम्
अन्धकानुग्रहं चैव मन्दरे शोषणं तथा ॥
1.93.m: You ought to tell us what took place, as it was heard [by you], / both the grace shown to Andhaka and the drying up at Mandara."

1.93.s:
varalābhamaśeṣaṃ ca pravadāmi samāsataḥ
hiraṇyākṣasya tanayo hiraṇyanayanopamaḥ //
1.93.d:
वरलाभमशेषं च प्रवदामि समासतः
हिरण्याक्षस्य तनयो हिरण्यनयनोपमः ॥
1.93.m: "I shall declare concisely the complete attainment of the boon: / The son of Hiraṇyākṣa, resembling the golden-eyed one,

1.93.s:
purāndhaka iti khyātas tapasā labdhavikramaḥ
prasādādbrahmaṇaḥ sākṣād avadhyatvamavāpya ca //
1.93.d:
पुरान्धक इति ख्यातस् तपसा लब्धविक्रमः
प्रसादाद्ब्रह्मणः साक्षाद् अवध्यत्वमवाप्य च ॥
1.93.m: celebrated of old as Andhaka, who gained prowess through austerity, / having obtained invulnerability directly by the grace of Brahmā,

1.93.s:
trailokyamakhilaṃ bhuktvā jitvā cendrapuraṃ purā
līlayā cāprayatnena trāsayāmāsa vāsavam //
1.93.d:
त्रैलोक्यमखिलं भुक्त्वा जित्वा चेन्द्रपुरं पुरा
लीलया चाप्रयत्नेन त्रासयामास वासवम् ॥
1.93.m: enjoyed the entire three worlds and conquered the city of Indra of old, / and playfully, without effort, terrified Indra.

1.93.s:
bādhitāstāḍitā baddhāḥ pātitāstena te surāḥ
viviśurmandaraṃ bhītā nārāyaṇapurogamāḥ //
1.93.d:
बाधितास्ताडिता बद्धाः पातितास्तेन ते सुराः
विविशुर्मन्दरं भीता नारायणपुरोगमाः ॥
1.93.m: Oppressed, beaten, bound, and struck down by him, / the gods, terrified, entered Mandara with Nārāyaṇa at their head.

1.93.s:
evaṃ saṃpīḍya vai devān andhako 'pi mahāsuraḥ
yadṛcchayā giriṃ prāpto mandaraṃ cārukandaram //
1.93.d:
एवं संपीड्य वै देवान् अन्धको ऽपि महासुरः
यदृच्छया गिरिं प्राप्तो मन्दरं चारुकन्दरम् ॥
1.93.m: Having thus tormented the gods, the great asura Andhaka / also happened to reach the mountain Mandara, of beautiful caves.

1.93.s:
tataste samastāḥ surendrāḥ sasādhyāḥ sureśaṃ maheśaṃ puretyāhurevam
drutaṃ cālpavīryaprabhinnāṅgabhinnā vayaṃ daityarājasya śastrairnikṛttāḥ //
1.93.d:
ततस्ते समस्ताः सुरेन्द्राः ससाध्याः सुरेशं महेशं पुरेत्याहुरेवम्
द्रुतं चाल्पवीर्यप्रभिन्नाङ्गभिन्ना वयं दैत्यराजस्य शस्त्रैर्निकृत्ताः ॥
1.93.m: Then all those lords of gods together with the sādhyas said to Maheśa, lord of gods, approaching him: / 'Quickly, our bodies shattered by diminished strength, we are cut to pieces by the daitya king's weapons.'

1.93.s:
itīdamakhilaṃ śrutvā daityāgamam anaupamam
gaṇeśvaraiś ca bhagavān andhakābhimukhaṃ yayau //
1.93.d:
इतीदमखिलं श्रुत्वा दैत्यागमम् अनौपमम्
गणेश्वरैश् च भगवान् अन्धकाभिमुखं ययौ ॥
1.93.m: Hearing this entire report of the peerless arrival of the daitya, / the Lord went towards Andhaka accompanied by the lords of the gaṇas.

1.93.s: jayeti vācā bhagavantam ūcuḥ kirīṭabaddhāñjalayaḥ samantāt //
1.93.d: जयेति वाचा भगवन्तम् ऊचुः किरीटबद्धाञ्जलयः समन्तात् ॥
1.93.m: With crowns bowed and palms joined on all sides, they said to the Lord with the word, 'Victory!'

1.93.s:
athāśeṣāsurāṃstasya koṭikoṭiśatais tataḥ
bhasmīkṛtya mahādevo nirbibhedāndhakaṃ tadā //
1.93.d:
अथाशेषासुरांस्तस्य कोटिकोटिशतैस् ततः
भस्मीकृत्य महादेवो निर्बिभेदान्धकं तदा ॥
1.93.m: Then, having reduced all his asuras to ashes by hundreds of crores, / Mahādeva pierced Andhaka.

1.93.s:
śūlena śūlinā protaṃ dagdhakalmaṣakañcukam
dṛṣṭvāndhakaṃ nanādeśaṃ praṇamya sa pitāmahaḥ //
1.93.d:
शूलेन शूलिना प्रोतं दग्धकल्मषकञ्चुकम्
दृष्ट्वान्धकं ननादेशं प्रणम्य स पितामहः ॥
1.93.m: Seeing Andhaka impaled on the trident by the trident-bearer, his armour of defilement burned away, / Pitāmaha bowed down and shouted praises to the Lord.

1.93.s:
tannādaśravaṇānnedur devā devaṃ praṇamya tam
nanṛturmunayaḥ sarve mumudurgaṇapuṅgavāḥ //
1.93.d:
तन्नादश्रवणान्नेदुर् देवा देवं प्रणम्य तम्
ननृतुर्मुनयः सर्वे मुमुदुर्गणपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.93.m: Hearing that shout, the gods bowed down to that god and roared; / all the sages danced, and the foremost gaṇas rejoiced.

1.93.s:
sasṛjuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi devāḥ śaṃbhostadopari
trailokyamakhilaṃ harṣān nananda ca nanāda ca //
1.93.d:
ससृजुः पुष्पवर्षाणि देवाः शंभोस्तदोपरि
त्रैलोक्यमखिलं हर्षान् ननन्द च ननाद च ॥
1.93.m: The gods showered rainfalls of flowers upon Śambhu; / out of joy, the entire threefold world exulted and roared.

1.93.s:
dagdho 'gninā ca śūlena protaḥ preta ivāndhakaḥ
sāttvikaṃ bhāvamāsthāya cintayāmāsa cetasā //
1.93.d:
दग्धो ऽग्निना च शूलेन प्रोतः प्रेत इवान्धकः
सात्त्विकं भावमास्थाय चिन्तयामास चेतसा ॥
1.93.m: Burned by fire and impaled on the trident like a ghost, Andhaka, / adopting a sattva-filled disposition, thought in his mind:

1.93.s:
janmāntare 'pi devena dagdho yasmācchivena vai
ārādhito mayā śaṃbhuḥ purā sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ //
1.93.d:
जन्मान्तरे ऽपि देवेन दग्धो यस्माच्छिवेन वै
आराधितो मया शंभुः पुरा साक्षान्महेश्वरः ॥
1.93.m: 'Because I am burned by the god Śiva, even in another life / Śambhu, the manifest Maheśvara, was worshipped by me of old.

1.93.s:
tasmādetanmayā labdham anyathā nopapadyate
yaḥ smarenmanasā rudraṃ prāṇānte sakṛdeva vā //
1.93.d:
तस्मादेतन्मया लब्धम् अन्यथा नोपपद्यते
यः स्मरेन्मनसा रुद्रं प्राणान्ते सकृदेव वा ॥
1.93.m: Therefore this has been obtained by me; otherwise it would not be possible. / Whoever remembers Rudra with his mind even once at the end of life,

1.93.s:
sa yāti śivasāyujyaṃ kiṃ punarbahuśaḥ smaran
brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ //
1.93.d:
स याति शिवसायुज्यं किं पुनर्बहुशः स्मरन्
ब्रह्मा च भगवान्विष्णुः सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ॥
1.93.m: attains intimate union with Śiva; how much more so one who remembers him repeatedly? / Brahmā and the blessed Viṣṇu, and all the gods together with Indra,

1.93.s:
śaraṇaṃ prāpya tiṣṭhanti tameva śaraṇaṃ vrajet
evaṃ saṃcintya tuṣṭātmā so 'ndhakaś cāndhakārdanam //
1.93.d:
शरणं प्राप्य तिष्ठन्ति तमेव शरणं व्रजेत्
एवं संचिन्त्य तुष्टात्मा सो ऽन्धकश् चान्धकार्दनम् ॥
1.93.m: abide having taken refuge; one should seek refuge in him alone.' / Thinking thus, his mind pleased, that Andhaka praised the destroyer of Andhaka,

1.93.s:
sagaṇaṃ śivamīśānam astuvatpuṇyagauravāt
prārthitastena bhagavān paramārtiharo haraḥ //
1.93.d:
सगणं शिवमीशानम् अस्तुवत्पुण्यगौरवात्
प्रार्थितस्तेन भगवान् परमार्तिहरो हरः ॥
1.93.m: Śiva, Īśāna, along with his gaṇa, through the gravity of merit. / Prayed to by him, the Lord Hara, remover of supreme distress,

1.93.s:
hiraṇyanetratanayaṃ śūlāgrasthaṃ sureśvaraḥ
provāca dānavaṃ prekṣya ghṛṇayā nīlalohitaḥ //
1.93.d:
हिरण्यनेत्रतनयं शूलाग्रस्थं सुरेश्वरः
प्रोवाच दानवं प्रेक्ष्य घृणया नीललोहितः ॥
1.93.m: the Lord of gods, Nīlalohita, looking out of pity at the dānava, / the son of Hiraṇyanetra situated on the tip of the trident, said:

1.93.s:
tuṣṭo 'smi vatsa bhadraṃ te kāmaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi te
varānvaraya daityendra varado 'haṃ tavāndhaka //
1.93.d:
तुष्टो ऽस्मि वत्स भद्रं ते कामं किं करवाणि ते
वरान्वरय दैत्येन्द्र वरदो ऽहं तवान्धक ॥
1.93.m: 'I am pleased, my child; blessing upon you! What desire of yours may I fulfil? / Choose boons, O lord of daityas; I am the giver of boons to you, O Andhaka.'

1.93.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ tadā śaṃbhor hiraṇyanayanātmajaḥ
harṣagadgadayā vācā provācedaṃ maheśvaram //
1.93.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं तदा शंभोर् हिरण्यनयनात्मजः
हर्षगद्गदया वाचा प्रोवाचेदं महेश्वरम् ॥
1.93.m: Hearing the words of Śambhu, the son of the golden-eyed one / said this to Maheśvara in a voice faltering with joy:

1.93.s:
bhagavandevadeveśa bhaktārtihara śaṅkara
tvayi bhaktiḥ prasīdeśa yadi deyo varaś ca me //
1.93.d:
भगवन्देवदेवेश भक्तार्तिहर शङ्कर
त्वयि भक्तिः प्रसीदेश यदि देयो वरश् च मे ॥
1.93.m:
"O Lord, Lord of the gods of gods, dispeller of the distress of devotees, Śaṅkara,
if a boon is to be given to me, be pleased, O Lord: [let there be] devotion to you!"

1.93.s:
śrutvā bhavo 'pi vacanam andhakasya mahātmanaḥ
pradadau durlabhāṃ śraddhāṃ daityendrāya mahādyutiḥ //
1.93.d:
श्रुत्वा भवो ऽपि वचनम् अन्धकस्य महात्मनः
प्रददौ दुर्लभां श्रद्धां दैत्येन्द्राय महाद्युतिः ॥
1.93.m:
Having heard the words of the high-souled Andhaka,
Bhava, of great splendour, granted rare faith to the lord of the Daityas.

1.93.s:
gāṇapatyaṃ ca daityāya pradadau cāvaropya tam
praṇemustaṃ surendrādyā gāṇapatye pratiṣṭhitam //
1.93.d:
गाणपत्यं च दैत्याय प्रददौ चावरोप्य तम्
प्रणेमुस्तं सुरेन्द्राद्या गाणपत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
1.93.m:
And bringing him down, he granted leadership of the gaṇas to the Daitya;
established in the leadership of the gaṇas, the lords of the gods and others bowed to him.

1.94.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathamasya pitā daityo hiraṇyākṣaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
viṣṇunā sūdito viṣṇur vārāhatvaṃ kathaṃ gataḥ //
1.94.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथमस्य पिता दैत्यो हिरण्याक्षः सुदारुणः
विष्णुना सूदितो विष्णुर् वाराहत्वं कथं गतः ॥
1.94.m:
The sages said:
How was his father, the most fierce Daitya Hiraṇyākṣa,
slain by Viṣṇu? How did Viṣṇu assume the state of a boar?

1.94.s:
tasya śṛṅgaṃ maheśasya bhūṣaṇatvaṃ kathaṃ gatam
etatsarvaṃ viśeṣeṇa sūta vaktumihārhasi //
1.94.d:
तस्य शृङ्गं महेशस्य भूषणत्वं कथं गतम्
एतत्सर्वं विशेषेण सूत वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
1.94.m:
How did his tusk become an ornament for Maheśa?
O Sūta, you ought to tell all this in detail here.

1.94.s:
sūta uvāca
hiraṇyakaśiporbhrātā hiraṇyākṣa iti smṛtaḥ
purāndhakāsureśasya pitā kālāntakopamaḥ //
1.94.d:
सूत उवाच
हिरण्यकशिपोर्भ्राता हिरण्याक्ष इति स्मृतः
पुरान्धकासुरेशस्य पिता कालान्तकोपमः ॥

1.94.s:
devāñjitvātha daityendro baddhvā ca dharaṇīmimām
nītvā rasātalaṃ cakre vandīm indīvaraprabhām //
1.94.d:
देवाञ्जित्वाथ दैत्येन्द्रो बद्ध्वा च धरणीमिमाम्
नीत्वा रसातलं चक्रे वन्दीम् इन्दीवरप्रभाम् ॥
1.94.m:
Then, having conquered the gods and bound this earth,
the lord of the Daityas took her to Rasātala and made a captive of her who has the lustre of a blue lotus.

1.94.s:
tataḥ sabrahmakā devāḥ parimlānamukhaśriyaḥ
bādhitāstāḍitā baddhvā hiraṇyākṣeṇa tena vai //
1.94.d:
ततः सब्रह्मका देवाः परिम्लानमुखश्रियः
बाधितास्ताडिता बद्ध्वा हिरण्याक्षेण तेन वै ॥
1.94.m:
Then the gods, together with Brahmā, the splendour of their faces faded,
oppressed, beaten, and bound indeed by that Hiraṇyākṣa,

1.94.s:
balinā daityamukhyena krūreṇa sudurātmanā
praṇamya śirasā viṣṇuṃ daityakoṭivimardanam //
1.94.d:
बलिना दैत्यमुख्येन क्रूरेण सुदुरात्मना
प्रणम्य शिरसा विष्णुं दैत्यकोटिविमर्दनम् ॥
1.94.m:
by that mighty leader of the Daityas, cruel and exceedingly wicked-minded,
bowed with their heads to Viṣṇu, the crusher of tens of millions of Daityas.

1.94.s:
sarve vijñāpayāmāsur dharaṇībandhanaṃ hareḥ
śrutvaitadbhagavān viṣṇur dharaṇībandhanaṃ hariḥ //
1.94.d:
सर्वे विज्ञापयामासुर् धरणीबन्धनं हरेः
श्रुत्वैतद्भगवान् विष्णुर् धरणीबन्धनं हरिः ॥
1.94.m:
They all reported the binding of the earth to Hari.
Hearing this binding of the earth, the Blessed Viṣṇu, Hari,

1.94.s:
bhūtvā yajñavarāho 'sau yathā liṅgodbhave tathā
daityaiś ca sārdhaṃ daityendraṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ mahābalam //
1.94.d:
भूत्वा यज्ञवराहो ऽसौ यथा लिङ्गोद्भवे तथा
दैत्यैश् च सार्धं दैत्येन्द्रं हिरण्याक्षं महाबलम् ॥
1.94.m:
having become the Boar of Sacrifice—just as at the manifestation of the liṅga—
[encountered] the exceedingly powerful lord of the Daityas, Hiraṇyākṣa, along with the Daityas.

1.94.s:
daṃṣṭrāgrakoṭyā hatvainaṃ reje daityāntakṛtprabhuḥ
kalpādiṣu yathāpūrvaṃ praviśya ca rasātalam //
1.94.d:
दंष्ट्राग्रकोट्या हत्वैनं रेजे दैत्यान्तकृत्प्रभुः
कल्पादिषु यथापूर्वं प्रविश्य च रसातलम् ॥
1.94.m:
Having slain him with the tip of his sharp tusk, the Lord, the destroyer of Daityas, shone resplendent.
And entering Rasātala as before at the beginning of the kalpas,

1.94.s:
ānīya vasudhāṃ devīm aṅkasthāmakarodbahiḥ
tatas tuṣṭāva deveśaṃ devadevaḥ pitāmahaḥ //
1.94.d:
आनीय वसुधां देवीम् अङ्कस्थामकरोद्बहिः
ततस् तुष्टाव देवेशं देवदेवः पितामहः ॥
1.94.m:
bringing the goddess Earth, he placed her on his lap outside.
Then Pitāmaha, the god of gods, praised the Lord of the gods,

1.94.s:
śakrādyaiḥ sahito bhūtvā harṣagadgadayā girā
śāśvatāya varāhāya daṃṣṭriṇe daṇḍine namaḥ //
1.94.d:
शक्राद्यैः सहितो भूत्वा हर्षगद्गदया गिरा
शाश्वताय वराहाय दंष्ट्रिणे दण्डिने नमः ॥
1.94.m:
joined by Śakra and the others, with a voice faltering with joy:
"Obeisance to the eternal Boar, the tusker, the staff-bearer!

1.94.s:
nārāyaṇāya sarvāya brahmaṇe paramātmane
kartre dhartre dharāyāstu hartre devāriṇāṃ svayam
kartre netre surendrāṇāṃ śāstre ca sakalasya ca //
1.94.d:
नारायणाय सर्वाय ब्रह्मणे परमात्मने
कर्त्रे धर्त्रे धरायास्तु हर्त्रे देवारिणां स्वयम्
कर्त्रे नेत्रे सुरेन्द्राणां शास्त्रे च सकलस्य च ॥
1.94.m:
To Nārāyaṇa, to Sarva, to Brahman, to the Supreme Self,
the maker and sustainer of the earth, the slayer of the foes of the gods himself,
the maker and guide of the lords of the gods, and the ruler of all!

1.94.s:
tvamaṣṭamūrtistvamanantamūrtis tvamādidevastvamanantaveditaḥ
tvayā kṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ prasīda sureśa lokeśa varāha viṣṇo //
1.94.d:
त्वमष्टमूर्तिस्त्वमनन्तमूर्तिस् त्वमादिदेवस्त्वमनन्तवेदितः
त्वया कृतं सर्वमिदं प्रसीद सुरेश लोकेश वराह विष्णो ॥
1.94.m:
You are the eight-formed one, you are the endless-formed one, you are the primal god, you are known through endless [texts];
all this was made by you; be gracious, O Lord of the gods, Lord of the world, O Boar, O Viṣṇu!

1.94.s:
tathaikadaṃṣṭrāgramukhāgrakoṭibhāgaikabhāgārdhatamena viṣṇo
hatāḥ kṣaṇāt kāmada daityamukhyāḥ svadaṃṣṭrakoṭyā saha putrabhṛtyaiḥ //
1.94.d:
तथैकदंष्ट्राग्रमुखाग्रकोटिभागैकभागार्धतमेन विष्णो
हताः क्षणात् कामद दैत्यमुख्याः स्वदंष्ट्रकोट्या सह पुत्रभृत्यैः ॥
1.94.m:
Likewise, O Viṣṇu, by a mere half-fraction of the front edge of the tip of a single tusk,
the foremost Daityas, together with their sons and servants, were slain in an instant, O granter of desires, by the tip of your tusk!

1.94.s:
tvayoddhṛtā deva dharā dhareśa dharādharākāra dhṛtāgradaṃṣṭre
dharādharaiḥ sarvajanaiḥ samudraiḥ surāsuraiḥ sevitacandravaktra //
1.94.d:
त्वयोद्धृता देव धरा धरेश धराधराकार धृताग्रदंष्ट्रे
धराधरैः सर्वजनैः समुद्रैः सुरासुरैः सेवितचन्द्रवक्त्र ॥
1.94.m:
By you, O God, Lord of the earth, bearing the form of a mountain, holding [her] on the tip of your tusk, the earth was lifted up,
O you whose moon-like face is attended by mountains, by all people, by oceans, by gods and Asuras!

1.94.s:
tvayaiva deveśa vibho kṛtaś ca jayaḥ surāṇāmasureśvarāṇām
aho pradattastu varaḥ prasīda vāgdevatā vārijasaṃbhavāya //
1.94.d:
त्वयैव देवेश विभो कृतश् च जयः सुराणामसुरेश्वराणाम्
अहो प्रदत्तस्तु वरः प्रसीद वाग्देवता वारिजसंभवाय ॥
1.94.m:
By you alone, O Lord of the gods, O omnipresent one, was victory wrought for the gods over the lords of the Asuras;
oh, a boon was granted to the lotus-born one [Brahmā] and the goddess of speech; be pleased!

1.94.s: nihitā rasātalagatā vasuṃdharā tava pṛṣṭhataḥ sakalatārakādayaḥ //
1.94.d: निहिता रसातलगता वसुंधरा तव पृष्ठतः सकलतारकादयः ॥
1.94.m: The earth that had gone to Rasātala was deposited [by you]; upon your back are all the stars and heavenly bodies.

1.94.s:
jagatāṃ hitāya bhavatā vasuṃdharā bhagavan rasātalapuṭaṃ gatā tadā
abaloddhṛtā ca bhagavaṃstavaiva sakalaṃ tvayaiva hi dhṛtaṃ jagadguro //
1.94.d:
जगतां हिताय भवता वसुंधरा भगवन् रसातलपुटं गता तदा
अबलोद्धृता च भगवंस्तवैव सकलं त्वयैव हि धृतं जगद्गुरो ॥
1.94.m:
For the welfare of the worlds, O Blessed One, the earth, which had then reached the hollow of Rasātala,
was lifted up by you, the powerless [rescued]; all is indeed yours, for by you alone is it sustained, O Guru of the world!

1.94.s:
iti vākpatirbahuvidhaistavārcanaiḥ praṇipatya viṣṇumamaraiḥ prajāpatiḥ
vividhānvarān harimukhāttu labdhavān harinābhivārijadehabhṛt svayam //
1.94.d:
इति वाक्पतिर्बहुविधैस्तवार्चनैः प्रणिपत्य विष्णुममरैः प्रजापतिः
विविधान्वरान् हरिमुखात्तु लब्धवान् हरिनाभिवारिजदेहभृत् स्वयम् ॥
1.94.m:
Thus Prajāpati, the lord of speech, having bowed to Viṣṇu together with the immortals through many kinds of praise and worship,
obtained various boons from the mouth of Hari, he who himself bears a body born from the lotus of Hari's navel."

1.94.s:
atha tāmuddhṛtāṃ tena dharāṃ devā munīśvarāḥ
mūrdhnyāropya namaścakruś cakriṇaḥ saṃnidhau tadā //
1.94.d:
अथ तामुद्धृतां तेन धरां देवा मुनीश्वराः
मूर्ध्न्यारोप्य नमश्चक्रुश् चक्रिणः संनिधौ तदा ॥
1.94.m:
Then the gods and the foremost of sages placed on their heads that earth
lifted up by him, and bowed in the presence of the discus-bearer.

1.94.s:
anenaiva varāheṇa coddhṛtāsi varaprade
kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakāryeṇa śatahastena viṣṇunā //
1.94.d:
अनेनैव वराहेण चोद्धृतासि वरप्रदे
कृष्णेनाक्लिष्टकार्येण शतहस्तेन विष्णुना ॥
1.94.m:
"You have been lifted up by this very Boar, O granter of boons,
by Kṛṣṇa of effortless deeds, by Viṣṇu of a hundred arms.

1.94.s:
dharaṇi tvaṃ mahābhoge bhūmistvaṃ dhenuravyaye
lokānāṃ dhāriṇī tvaṃ hi mṛttike hara pātakam //
1.94.d:
धरणि त्वं महाभोगे भूमिस्त्वं धेनुरव्यये
लोकानां धारिणी त्वं हि मृत्तिके हर पातकम् ॥
1.94.m:
O Earth, you of great enjoyment, you are the soil, you are the cow, O imperishable one,
you are indeed the supporter of the worlds; O earth-clay, remove our sin!

1.94.s:
manasā karmaṇā vācā varade vārijekṣaṇe
tvayā hatena pāpena jīvāmastvatprasādataḥ //
1.94.d:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा वरदे वारिजेक्षणे
त्वया हतेन पापेन जीवामस्त्वत्प्रसादतः ॥
1.94.m:
In thought, word, and deed, O granter of boons, lotus-eyed one,
with our sin destroyed by you, we live through your grace!"

1.94.s:
ityuktā sā tadā devī dharā devair athābravīt
varāhadaṃṣṭrābhinnāyāṃ dharāyāṃ mṛttikāṃ dvijāḥ //
1.94.d:
इत्युक्ता सा तदा देवी धरा देवैर् अथाब्रवीत्
वराहदंष्ट्राभिन्नायां धरायां मृत्तिकां द्विजाः ॥
1.94.m:
Thus addressed then by the gods, the goddess Earth said:
"O twice-born ones, whoever applies to his head, with this mantra,

1.94.s:
mantreṇānena yo bibhrat mūrdhni pāpātpramucyate
āyuṣmān balavān dhanyaḥ putrapautrasamanvitaḥ //
1.94.d:
मन्त्रेणानेन यो बिभ्रत् मूर्ध्नि पापात्प्रमुच्यते
आयुष्मान् बलवान् धन्यः पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वितः ॥
1.94.m:
the clay from the earth split open by the Boar's tusk, is released from sin;
he becomes long-lived, strong, blessed, and endowed with sons and grandsons.

1.94.s:
kramādbhuvi divaṃ prāpya karmānte modate suraiḥ
atha deve gate tyaktvā varāhe kṣīrasāgaram //
1.94.d:
क्रमाद्भुवि दिवं प्राप्य कर्मान्ते मोदते सुरैः
अथ देवे गते त्यक्त्वा वराहे क्षीरसागरम् ॥
1.94.m:
In due course, leaving the earth and attaining heaven, he rejoices with the gods at the end of his deeds."
Then, when the god, the Boar, had departed, leaving the ocean of milk,

1.94.s:
vārāharūpamanaghaṃ cacāla ca dharā punaḥ
tasya daṃṣṭrābharākrāntā devadevasya dhīmataḥ //
1.94.d:
वाराहरूपमनघं चचाल च धरा पुनः
तस्य दंष्ट्राभराक्रान्ता देवदेवस्य धीमतः ॥
1.94.m:
and [leaving behind] his faultless boar form, the earth shook again,
oppressed by the weight of the tusk of that wise god of gods.

1.94.s:
yadṛcchayā bhavaḥ paśyan jagāma jagadīśvaraḥ
daṃṣṭrāṃ jagrāha dṛṣṭvā tāṃ bhūṣaṇārthamathātmanaḥ //
1.94.d:
यदृच्छया भवः पश्यन् जगाम जगदीश्वरः
दंष्ट्रां जग्राह दृष्ट्वा तां भूषणार्थमथात्मनः ॥
1.94.m:
Passing by by chance and seeing it, Bhava, the Lord of the world,
seeing that tusk, seized it as an ornament for himself.

1.94.s:
dadhāra ca mahādevaḥ kūrcānte vai mahorasi
devāś ca tuṣṭuvuḥ sendrā devadevasya vaibhavam //
1.94.d:
दधार च महादेवः कूर्चान्ते वै महोरसि
देवाश् च तुष्टुवुः सेन्द्रा देवदेवस्य वैभवम् ॥
1.94.m:
And Mahādeva wore it at the end of his beard upon his broad chest;
and the gods, led by Indra, praised the majesty of the god of gods.

1.94.s:
dharā pratiṣṭhitā hyevaṃ devadevena līlayā
bhūtānāṃ saṃplave cāpi viṣṇoścaiva kalevaram //
1.94.d:
धरा प्रतिष्ठिता ह्येवं देवदेवेन लीलया
भूतानां संप्लवे चापि विष्णोश्चैव कलेवरम् ॥
1.94.m:
Thus was the earth stabilized by the god of gods in divine play;
and at the deluge of all beings, [he wears] the body of Viṣṇu,

1.94.s:
brahmaṇaś ca tathānyeṣāṃ devānāmapi līlayā
vibhuraṅgavibhāgena bhūṣito na yadi prabhuḥ //
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मणश् च तथान्येषां देवानामपि लीलया
विभुरङ्गविभागेन भूषितो न यदि प्रभुः ॥
1.94.m:
and likewise of Brahmā and of other gods, in divine play.
If the all-pervading Lord were not adorned with parts of their bodies,

1.94.s: kathaṃ vimuktirviprāṇāṃ tasmāddaṃṣṭrī maheśvaraḥ //
1.94.d: कथं विमुक्तिर्विप्राणां तस्माद्दंष्ट्री महेश्वरः ॥
1.94.m: how could there be liberation for the brahmins? Therefore Maheśvara bears the tusk.

1.95.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
nṛsiṃhena hataḥ pūrvaṃ hiraṇyākṣāgrajaḥ śrutam
kathaṃ niṣūditastena hiraṇyakaśipurvada //
1.95.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
नृसिंहेन हतः पूर्वं हिरण्याक्षाग्रजः श्रुतम्
कथं निषूदितस्तेन हिरण्यकशिपुर्वद ॥
1.95.m:
The sages said:
It has been heard that the elder brother of Hiraṇyākṣa was slain formerly by the Man-Lion.
Tell us how Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain by him.

1.95.s:
sūta uvāca
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putraḥ prahrāda iti viśrutaḥ
dharmajñaḥ satyasampannas tapasvī cābhavatsudhīḥ //
1.95.d:
सूत उवाच
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्रः प्रह्राद इति विश्रुतः
धर्मज्ञः सत्यसम्पन्नस् तपस्वी चाभवत्सुधीः ॥
1.95.m:
Sūta said:
Hiraṇyakaśipu had a son renowned as Prahrāda,
who knew dharma, was endowed with truth, was an ascetic, and was wise.

1.95.s:
janmaprabhṛti deveśaṃ pūjayāmāsa cāvyayam
sarvajñaṃ sarvagaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvadevabhavodbhavam //
1.95.d:
जन्मप्रभृति देवेशं पूजयामास चाव्ययम्
सर्वज्ञं सर्वगं विष्णुं सर्वदेवभवोद्भवम् ॥
1.95.m:
From his very birth, he worshipped the imperishable Lord of the gods,
the omniscient, all-pervading Viṣṇu, the origin of the birth of all gods,

1.95.s:
tamādipuruṣaṃ bhaktyā parabrahmasvarūpiṇam
brahmaṇo 'dhipatiṃ sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārakāraṇam //
1.95.d:
तमादिपुरुषं भक्त्या परब्रह्मस्वरूपिणम्
ब्रह्मणो ऽधिपतिं सृष्टिस्थितिसंहारकारणम् ॥
1.95.m:
him, the primal Puruṣa, the embodiment of the supreme Brahman, with devotion—
the ruler of Brahmā, the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

1.95.s:
so 'pi viṣṇostathābhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā putraṃ samāhitam
namo nārāyaṇāyeti govindeti muhurmuhuḥ //
1.95.d:
सो ऽपि विष्णोस्तथाभूतं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रं समाहितम्
नमो नारायणायेति गोविन्देति मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
1.95.m:
Seeing his son composed thus toward Viṣṇu,
praising him constantly with, "Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa! O Govinda!",

1.95.s:
stuvantaṃ prāha devāriḥ pradahanniva pāpadhīḥ
na māṃ jānāsi durbuddhe sarvadaityāmareśvaram //
1.95.d:
स्तुवन्तं प्राह देवारिः प्रदहन्निव पापधीः
न मां जानासि दुर्बुद्धे सर्वदैत्यामरेश्वरम् ॥
1.95.m:
the enemy of the gods, evil-minded, spoke as though burning him:
"Do you not know me, O fool, as the lord of all Daityas and immortals?

1.95.s:
prahrāda vīra duṣputra dvijadevārtikāraṇam
ko viṣṇuḥ padmajo vāpi śakraś ca varuṇo 'thavā //
1.95.d:
प्रह्राद वीर दुष्पुत्र द्विजदेवार्तिकारणम्
को विष्णुः पद्मजो वापि शक्रश् च वरुणो ऽथवा ॥
1.95.m:
O Prahrāda, warrior, wicked son, cause of distress to twice-born and gods!
Who is Viṣṇu, or the lotus-born [Brahmā], or Śakra, or Varuṇa,

1.95.s:
vāyuḥ somastatheśānaḥ pāvako mama yaḥ samaḥ
māmevārcaya bhaktyā ca svalpaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ sadā //
1.95.d:
वायुः सोमस्तथेशानः पावको मम यः समः
मामेवार्चय भक्त्या च स्वल्पं नारायणं सदा ॥
1.95.m:
or Vāyu, or Soma, or Īśāna, or Fire, that is equal to me?
Worship me alone with devotion, and [regard] Nārāyaṇa ever as insignificant!

1.95.s:
prahrāda jīvite vāñchā tavaiṣā śṛṇu cāsti cet
śrutvāpi tasya vacanaṃ hiraṇyakaśipoḥ sudhīḥ //
1.95.d:
प्रह्राद जीविते वाञ्छा तवैषा शृणु चास्ति चेत्
श्रुत्वापि तस्य वचनं हिरण्यकशिपोः सुधीः ॥
1.95.m:
Hear this, O Prahrāda, if you have a desire for life!"
Even upon hearing those words of Hiraṇyakaśipu, the wise one—

1.95.s:
prahrādaḥ pūjayāmāsa namo nārāyaṇeti ca
namo nārāyaṇāyeti sarvadaityakumārakān //
1.95.d:
प्रह्रादः पूजयामास नमो नारायणेति च
नमो नारायणायेति सर्वदैत्यकुमारकान् ॥
1.95.m: Prahrāda worshipped, reciting, 'Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa!' / and to all the Daitya youths, 'Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa!'

1.95.s:
adhyāpayāmāsa ca tāṃ brahmavidyāṃ suśobhanām
durlaṅghyāṃ cātmano dṛṣṭvā śakrādibhir api svayam //
1.95.d:
अध्यापयामास च तां ब्रह्मविद्यां सुशोभनाम्
दुर्लङ्घ्यां चात्मनो दृष्ट्वा शक्रादिभिर् अपि स्वयम् ॥
1.95.m: He taught that most splendid knowledge of Brahman. / Seeing his own command flouted, which could not be crossed even by Śakra and the others,

1.95.s:
putreṇa laṅghitāmājñāṃ hiraṇyaḥ prāha dānavān
etaṃ nānāvidhairvadhyaṃ duṣputraṃ hantumarhatha //
1.95.d:
पुत्रेण लङ्घितामाज्ञां हिरण्यः प्राह दानवान्
एतं नानाविधैर्वध्यं दुष्पुत्रं हन्तुमर्हथ ॥
1.95.m: flouted by his son, Hiraṇya[kaśipu] said to the Dānavas: / 'You must slay this wicked son, fit to be killed in manifold ways!'

1.95.s:
evamuktāstadā tena daityena sudurātmanā
nijaghnurdevadevasya bhṛtyaṃ prahrādamavyayam //
1.95.d:
एवमुक्तास्तदा तेन दैत्येन सुदुरात्मना
निजघ्नुर्देवदेवस्य भृत्यं प्रह्रादमव्ययम् ॥
1.95.m: Thus addressed then by that utterly evil-minded Daitya, / they attacked the imperishable servant of the God of gods, Prahrāda.

1.95.s:
tatra tatpratikṛtaṃ tadā surair daityarājatanayaṃ dvijottamāḥ
kṣīravārinidhiśāyinaḥ prabhor niṣphalaṃ tvatha babhūva tejasā //
1.95.d:
तत्र तत्प्रतिकृतं तदा सुरैर् दैत्यराजतनयं द्विजोत्तमाः
क्षीरवारिनिधिशायिनः प्रभोर् निष्फलं त्वथ बभूव तेजसा ॥
1.95.m: Whatever countermeasures the gods [of the Daityas] took against the son of the Daitya king, O best of the twice-born, / became entirely fruitless through the splendour of the Lord who reclines on the ocean of milk.

1.95.s:
tadātha garvabhinnasya hiraṇyakaśipoḥ prabhuḥ
tatraivāvirabhūddhantuṃ nṛsiṃhākṛtimāsthitaḥ //
1.95.d:
तदाथ गर्वभिन्नस्य हिरण्यकशिपोः प्रभुः
तत्रैवाविरभूद्धन्तुं नृसिंहाकृतिमास्थितः ॥
1.95.m: Then, to Hiranyakaśipu whose pride was shattered, the Lord / manifested right there, assuming the form of Nṛsiṃha, to slay him.

1.95.s:
jaghāna ca sutaṃ prekṣya pitaraṃ dānavādhamam
bibheda tatkṣaṇādeva karajair niśitaiḥ śataiḥ //
1.95.d:
जघान च सुतं प्रेक्ष्य पितरं दानवाधमम्
बिभेद तत्क्षणादेव करजैर् निशितैः शतैः ॥
1.95.m: Seeing the son, he struck down the father, the vilest of the Dānavas; / he tore him apart in that very moment with hundreds of sharpened claws.

1.95.s:
tato nihatya taṃ daityaṃ sabāndhavamaghāpahaḥ
pīḍayāmāsa daityendraṃ yugāntāgnirivāparaḥ //
1.95.d:
ततो निहत्य तं दैत्यं सबान्धवमघापहः
पीडयामास दैत्येन्द्रं युगान्ताग्निरिवापरः ॥
1.95.m: Then, having slain that Daitya along with his kinsmen, the dispeller of sin / tormented the king of Daityas like another fire at the end of the yuga.

1.95.s:
nādaistasya nṛsiṃhasya ghorairvitrāsitaṃ jagat
ā brahmabhuvanād viprāḥ pracacāla ca suvratāḥ //
1.95.d:
नादैस्तस्य नृसिंहस्य घोरैर्वित्रासितं जगत्
आ ब्रह्मभुवनाद् विप्राः प्रचचाल च सुव्रताः ॥
1.95.m: By the terrible roars of that Nṛsiṃha the world was terrified; / it trembled from the realm of Brahmā downward, O upright Brahmins.

1.95.s:
dṛṣṭvā surāsuramahoragasiddhasādhyās tasmin kṣaṇe hariviriñcimukhā nṛsiṃham
dhairyaṃ balaṃ ca samavāpya yayurvisṛjya ā diṅmukhāntam asurakṣaṇatatparāś ca //
1.95.d:
दृष्ट्वा सुरासुरमहोरगसिद्धसाध्यास् तस्मिन् क्षणे हरिविरिञ्चिमुखा नृसिंहम्
धैर्यं बलं च समवाप्य ययुर्विसृज्य आ दिङ्मुखान्तम् असुरक्षणतत्पराश् च ॥
1.95.m: Seeing Nṛsiṃha at that moment, the gods, Asuras, great serpents, Siddhas, and Sādhyas, led by Hari and Viriñci, / abandoned their courage and strength and fled to the ends of the quarters, intent on their own preservation.

1.95.s:
tatastairgataiḥ saiṣa devo nṛsiṃhaḥ sahasrākṛtiḥ sarvapāt sarvabāhuḥ
sahasrekṣaṇaḥ somasūryāgninetras tadā saṃsthitaḥ sarvamāvṛtya māyī //
1.95.d:
ततस्तैर्गतैः सैष देवो नृसिंहः सहस्राकृतिः सर्वपात् सर्वबाहुः
सहस्रेक्षणः सोमसूर्याग्निनेत्रस् तदा संस्थितः सर्वमावृत्य मायी ॥
1.95.m: Then, when they had departed, that divine Nṛsiṃha—possessing a thousand forms, all feet, all arms, / possessing a thousand eyes, with moon, sun, and fire as eyes, the master of māyā—stood enclosing everything.

1.95.s:
taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ suraśreṣṭhā lokā lokācale sthitāḥ
sabrahmakāḥ sasādhyāś ca sayamāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ //
1.95.d:
तं तुष्टुवुः सुरश्रेष्ठा लोका लोकाचले स्थिताः
सब्रह्मकाः ससाध्याश् च सयमाः समरुद्गणाः ॥
1.95.m: The foremost gods dwelling on Mount Lokāloka praised him, / together with Brahmā, the Sādhyas, Yama, and the hosts of the Maruts:

1.95.s:
parātparataraṃ brahma tattvāt tattvatamaṃ bhavān
jyotiṣāṃ tu paraṃ jyotiḥ paramātmā jaganmayaḥ //
1.95.d:
परात्परतरं ब्रह्म तत्त्वात् तत्त्वतमं भवान्
ज्योतिषां तु परं ज्योतिः परमात्मा जगन्मयः ॥
1.95.m: 'You are the Brahman higher than the highest, the ultimate reality among principles, / the supreme light among lights, the Supreme Self consisting of the universe.

1.95.s:
sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ susūkṣmaṃ ca śabdabrahmamayaḥ śubhaḥ
vāgatīto nirālaṃbo nirdvandvo nirupaplavaḥ //
1.95.d:
स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं सुसूक्ष्मं च शब्दब्रह्ममयः शुभः
वागतीतो निरालंबो निर्द्वन्द्वो निरुपप्लवः ॥
1.95.m: You are the gross, the subtle, and the extremely subtle, the auspicious one composed of the sound-Brahman, / transcending speech, unsupported, beyond dualities, free from affliction.

1.95.s:
yajñabhugyajñamūrtistvaṃ yajñināṃ phaladaḥ prabhuḥ
bhavānmatsyākṛtiḥ kaurmam āsthāya jagati sthitaḥ //
1.95.d:
यज्ञभुग्यज्ञमूर्तिस्त्वं यज्ञिनां फलदः प्रभुः
भवान्मत्स्याकृतिः कौर्मम् आस्थाय जगति स्थितः ॥
1.95.m: You are the enjoyer of sacrifice, the sacrifice embodied, the lord who gives fruits to sacrificers. / Assuming the form of the Fish, and the form of the Tortoise, you abided in the world.

1.95.s:
vārāhīṃ caiva tāṃ saiṃhīm āsthāyehavyavasthitaḥ
devānāṃ devarakṣārthaṃ nihatya ditijeśvaram //
1.95.d:
वाराहीं चैव तां सैंहीम् आस्थायेहव्यवस्थितः
देवानां देवरक्षार्थं निहत्य दितिजेश्वरम् ॥
1.95.m: And assuming that Boar form, and now this Lion form, you stand established, / having slain the lord of Diti's sons to protect the gods of the gods.

1.95.s:
dvijaśāpacchalenaivam avatīrṇo 'si līlayā
na dṛṣṭaṃ yattvadanyaṃ hi bhavān sarvaṃ carācaram //
1.95.d:
द्विजशापच्छलेनैवम् अवतीर्णो ऽसि लीलया
न दृष्टं यत्त्वदन्यं हि भवान् सर्वं चराचरम् ॥
1.95.m: Under the pretext of a Brahmin's curse, you have descended thus in divine play; / for nothing other than you is seen—you are all that moves and is still.

1.95.s:
bhavānviṣṇurbhavān rudro bhavāneva pitāmahaḥ
bhavānādirbhavānanto bhavāneva vayaṃ vibho //
1.95.d:
भवान्विष्णुर्भवान् रुद्रो भवानेव पितामहः
भवानादिर्भवानन्तो भवानेव वयं विभो ॥
1.95.m: You are Viṣṇu, you are Rudra, you alone are Pitāmaha; / you are the beginning, you are the end, you alone are ourselves, O all-pervading Lord.

1.95.s:
bhavāneva jagatsarvaṃ pralāpena kimīśvara
māyayā bahudhā saṃstham advitīyamayaṃ prabho //
1.95.d:
भवानेव जगत्सर्वं प्रलापेन किमीश्वर
मायया बहुधा संस्थम् अद्वितीयमयं प्रभो ॥
1.95.m: You alone are the entire universe; what is the use of prattle, O Sovereign? / Established in manifold ways through māyā, you consist of the one without a second, O Lord.

1.95.s:
stoṣyāmastvāṃ kathaṃ bhāsi devadeva mṛgādhipa
stuto 'pi vividhaiḥ stutyair bhāvairnānāvidhaiḥ prabhuḥ //
1.95.d:
स्तोष्यामस्त्वां कथं भासि देवदेव मृगाधिप
स्तुतो ऽपि विविधैः स्तुत्यैर् भावैर्नानाविधैः प्रभुः ॥
1.95.m: How shall we praise you? You shine forth, O God of gods, king of beasts!' / Although praised with various laudable sentiments of many kinds, the Lord

1.95.s:
na jagāma dvijāḥ śāntiṃ mānayanyonimātmanaḥ
yo nṛsiṃhastavaṃ bhaktyā paṭhedvārthaṃ vicārayet //
1.95.d:
न जगाम द्विजाः शान्तिं मानयन्योनिमात्मनः
यो नृसिंहस्तवं भक्त्या पठेद्वार्थं विचारयेत् ॥
1.95.m: did not attain peace, O twice-born, honouring his lion origin. / Whoever recites the hymn to Nṛsiṃha with devotion, or contemplates its meaning,

1.95.s:
śrāvayedvā dvijānsarvān viṣṇuloke mahīyate
tadantare śivaṃ devāḥ sendrāḥ sabrahmakāḥ prabhum //
1.95.d:
श्रावयेद्वा द्विजान्सर्वान् विष्णुलोके महीयते
तदन्तरे शिवं देवाः सेन्द्राः सब्रह्मकाः प्रभुम् ॥
1.95.m: or recites it to all the Brahmins, is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu. / In the meantime, the gods, accompanied by Indra and Brahmā,

1.95.s:
samprāpya tuṣṭuvuḥ sarvaṃ vijñāpya mṛgarūpiṇaḥ
tato brahmādayastūrṇaṃ saṃstūya parameśvaram //
1.95.d:
सम्प्राप्य तुष्टुवुः सर्वं विज्ञाप्य मृगरूपिणः
ततो ब्रह्मादयस्तूर्णं संस्तूय परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.95.m: approached the Lord Śiva and praised him, reporting everything about the one who had taken the beast form. / Then Brahmā and the others, quickly praising the Supreme Lord,

1.95.s:
ātmatrāṇāya śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ paramakāraṇam
mandarasthaṃ mahādevaṃ krīḍamānaṃ sahomayā //
1.95.d:
आत्मत्राणाय शरणं जग्मुः परमकारणम्
मन्दरस्थं महादेवं क्रीडमानं सहोमया ॥
1.95.m: went for their own protection to the supreme cause as their refuge— / Mahādeva, who was staying on Mount Mandara, sporting with Umā,

1.95.s:
sevitaṃ gaṇagandharvaiḥ siddhairapsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
devatābhiḥ saha brahmā bhītabhītaḥ sagadgadam
praṇamya daṇḍavadbhūmau tuṣṭāva parameśvaram //
1.95.d:
सेवितं गणगन्धर्वैः सिद्धैरप्सरसां गणैः
देवताभिः सह ब्रह्मा भीतभीतः सगद्गदम्
प्रणम्य दण्डवद्भूमौ तुष्टाव परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.95.m: served by the Gaṇas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and hosts of Apsarases. / Brahmā, along with the deities, greatly terrified, faltering with emotion, / prostrating like a staff upon the ground, praised the Supreme Lord.

1.95.s:
brahmovāca
namaste kālakālāya namaste rudra manyave
namaḥ śivāya rudrāya śaṅkarāya śivāya te //
1.95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नमस्ते कालकालाय नमस्ते रुद्र मन्यवे
नमः शिवाय रुद्राय शङ्कराय शिवाय ते ॥
1.95.m: Brahmā said: / 'Obeisance to you, the Death of Death! Obeisance to you, O Rudra, wrath [personified]! / Obeisance to Śiva, to Rudra, to Śaṅkara, to the auspicious one!

1.95.s:
ugro 'si sarvabhūtānāṃ niyantāsi śivo 'si naḥ
namaḥ śivāya śarvāya śaṅkarāyārttihāriṇe //
1.95.d:
उग्रो ऽसि सर्वभूतानां नियन्तासि शिवो ऽसि नः
नमः शिवाय शर्वाय शङ्करायार्त्तिहारिणे ॥
1.95.m: You are fierce toward all creatures, you are their controller, you are benevolent to us. / Obeisance to Śiva, to Śarva, to Śaṅkara, to the remover of affliction!

1.95.s:
mayaskarāya viśvāya viṣṇave brahmaṇe namaḥ
antakāya namastubhyam umāyāḥ pataye namaḥ //
1.95.d:
मयस्कराय विश्वाय विष्णवे ब्रह्मणे नमः
अन्तकाय नमस्तुभ्यम् उमायाः पतये नमः ॥
1.95.m: Obeisance to the bringer of joy, to the all, to Viṣṇu, to Brahmā! / Obeisance to you, the end-maker; obeisance to the lord of Umā!

1.95.s:
hiraṇyabāhave sākṣād dhiraṇyapataye namaḥ
śarvāya sarvarūpāya puruṣāya namonamaḥ //
1.95.d:
हिरण्यबाहवे साक्षाद् धिरण्यपतये नमः
शर्वाय सर्वरूपाय पुरुषाय नमोनमः ॥
1.95.m: Obeisance to the golden-armed, visibly to the golden lord! / Obeisance, obeisance to Śarva, to the one whose form is everything, to Puruṣa!

1.95.s:
sadasadvyaktihīnāya mahataḥ kāraṇāya te
nityāya viśvarūpāya jāyamānāya te namaḥ //
1.95.d:
सदसद्व्यक्तिहीनाय महतः कारणाय ते
नित्याय विश्वरूपाय जायमानाय ते नमः ॥
1.95.m: To the one free from manifestation as existence or non-existence, to you the cause of the Great [Principle], / to the eternal, to the one whose form is the universe, to you who are being born, obeisance!

1.95.s:
jātāya bahudhā loke prabhūtāya namonamaḥ
rudrāya nīlarudrāya kadrudrāya pracetase //
1.95.d:
जाताय बहुधा लोके प्रभूताय नमोनमः
रुद्राय नीलरुद्राय कद्रुद्राय प्रचेतसे ॥
1.95.m: To the one born in manifold ways in the world, to the abundant one, obeisance, obeisance! / To Rudra, to Nīlarudra, to the auspicious Rudra, to the wise!

1.95.s:
kālāya kālarūpāya namaḥ kālāṅgahāriṇe
mīḍhuṣṭamāya devāya śitikaṇṭhāya te namaḥ //
1.95.d:
कालाय कालरूपाय नमः कालाङ्गहारिणे
मीढुष्टमाय देवाय शितिकण्ठाय ते नमः ॥
1.95.m: To Time, to the form of Time, obeisance to the destroyer of the limbs of Time! / To the most generous deity, to you of the dark neck, obeisance!

1.95.s:
mahīyase namastubhyaṃ hantre devāriṇāṃ sadā
tārāya ca sutārāya tāraṇāya namonamaḥ //
1.95.d:
महीयसे नमस्तुभ्यं हन्त्रे देवारिणां सदा
ताराय च सुताराय तारणाय नमोनमः ॥
1.95.m: Obeisance to you, the greatest, the eternal slayer of the enemies of the gods! / To the saviour, to the good deliverer, to the ferryman across [samsara], obeisance, obeisance!

1.95.s:
harikeśāya devāya śaṃbhave paramātmane
devānāṃ śaṃbhave tubhyaṃ bhūtānāṃ śaṃbhave namaḥ //
1.95.d:
हरिकेशाय देवाय शंभवे परमात्मने
देवानां शंभवे तुभ्यं भूतानां शंभवे नमः ॥
1.95.m: To the golden-haired god, to Śambhu, the Supreme Self; / to you, the Śambhu of the gods, to the Śambhu of all beings, obeisance!

1.95.s:
śambhave haimavatyāś ca manyave rudrarūpiṇe
kapardine namastubhyaṃ kālakaṇṭhāya te namaḥ //
1.95.d:
शम्भवे हैमवत्याश् च मन्यवे रुद्ररूपिणे
कपर्दिने नमस्तुभ्यं कालकण्ठाय ते नमः ॥
1.95.m: To the Śambhu of the daughter of Himavat, to the one whose form is wrath, Rudra! / To the one with matted hair, obeisance to you, to you with the black throat, obeisance!

1.95.s:
hiraṇyāya maheśāya śrīkaṇṭhāya namonamaḥ
bhasmadigdhaśarīrāya daṇḍamuṇḍīśvarāya ca //
1.95.d:
हिरण्याय महेशाय श्रीकण्ठाय नमोनमः
भस्मदिग्धशरीराय दण्डमुण्डीश्वराय च ॥
1.95.m: To the golden one, to the great lord, to Śrīkaṇṭha, obeisance, obeisance! / To the one whose body is smeared with sacred ash, to the lord with the staff and skull!

1.95.s:
namo hrasvāya dīrghāya vāmanāya namonamaḥ
nama ugratriśūlāya ugrāya ca namo namaḥ //
1.95.d:
नमो ह्रस्वाय दीर्घाय वामनाय नमोनमः
नम उग्रत्रिशूलाय उग्राय च नमो नमः ॥
1.95.m: Obeisance to the short, to the tall, to the dwarf, obeisance, obeisance! / Obeisance to the one with the fierce trident, and to the fierce one, obeisance, obeisance!

1.95.s:
bhīmāya bhīmarūpāya bhīmakarmaratāya te
agrevadhāya vai bhūtvā namo dūrevadhāya ca //
1.95.d:
भीमाय भीमरूपाय भीमकर्मरताय ते
अग्रेवधाय वै भूत्वा नमो दूरेवधाय च ॥
1.95.m: To the terrible, to the terrible in form, to you who delight in terrible deeds, / having become the slayer from up close, obeisance, and the slayer from afar!

1.95.s:
dhanvine śūline tubhyaṃ gadine haline namaḥ
cakriṇe varmiṇe nityaṃ daityānāṃ karmabhedine //
1.95.d:
धन्विने शूलिने तुभ्यं गदिने हलिने नमः
चक्रिणे वर्मिणे नित्यं दैत्यानां कर्मभेदिने ॥
1.95.m: To you, the archer, the bearer of the spear, the bearer of the mace, the bearer of the plough, obeisance! / To the bearer of the discus, to the armoured one, ever the shatterer of the Daityas' works!

1.95.s:
sadyāya sadyarūpāya sadyojātāya te namaḥ
vāmāya vāmarūpāya vāmanetrāya te namaḥ //
1.95.d:
सद्याय सद्यरूपाय सद्योजाताय ते नमः
वामाय वामरूपाय वामनेत्राय ते नमः ॥
1.95.m: To the immediate one, to the form of the immediate, to Sadyojāta, obeisance to you! / To the lovely one, to the lovely-formed, to you with lovely eyes, obeisance!

1.95.s: puruṣarūpāya puruṣaikatatpuruṣāya vai namaḥ //
1.95.d: पुरुषरूपाय पुरुषैकतत्पुरुषाय वै नमः ॥
1.95.m: Obeisance indeed to the form of Puruṣa, to the sole Puruṣa, to Tatpuruṣa!

1.95.s:
puruṣārthapradānāya pataye parameṣṭhine
īśānāya namastubhyam īśvarāya namonamaḥ //
1.95.d:
पुरुषार्थप्रदानाय पतये परमेष्ठिने
ईशानाय नमस्तुभ्यम् ईश्वराय नमोनमः ॥
1.95.m: To the bestower of the aims of human life, to the lord, to Parameṣṭhin! / To Īśāna, obeisance to you, to Īśvara, obeisance, obeisance!

1.95.s:
brahmaṇe brahmarūpāya namaḥ sākṣācchivāya te
sarvaviṣṇurnṛsiṃhasya rūpamāsthāya viśvakṛt //
1.95.d:
ब्रह्मणे ब्रह्मरूपाय नमः साक्षाच्छिवाय ते
सर्वविष्णुर्नृसिंहस्य रूपमास्थाय विश्वकृत् ॥
1.95.m: To Brahman, to the form of Brahman, obeisance to you, who are visibly Śiva! / The all-Viṣṇu, the creator of the universe, having assumed the form of Nṛsiṃha,

1.95.s:
hiraṇyakaśipuṃ hatvā karajairniśitaiḥ svayam
daityendrairbahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ hitārthaṃ jagatāṃ prabhuḥ //
1.95.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुं हत्वा करजैर्निशितैः स्वयम्
दैत्येन्द्रैर्बहुभिः सार्धं हितार्थं जगतां प्रभुः ॥
1.95.m: having himself slain Hiraṇyakaśipu with his sharpened claws, / along with many Daitya chiefs, for the welfare of the worlds, the Lord,

1.95.s:
saiṃhīṃ samānayanyoniṃ bādhate nikhilaṃ jagat
yatkṛtyamatra deveśa tatkuruṣva bhavāniha //
1.95.d:
सैंहीं समानयन्योनिं बाधते निखिलं जगत्
यत्कृत्यमत्र देवेश तत्कुरुष्व भवानिह ॥
1.95.m: honouring his lion origin, torments the entire universe. / Whatever is to be done in this matter, O Lord of gods, please do that here!

1.95.s:
ugro 'si sarvaduṣṭānāṃ niyantāsi śivo 'si naḥ
kālakūṭādivapuṣā trāhi naḥ śaraṇāgatān //
1.95.d:
उग्रो ऽसि सर्वदुष्टानां नियन्तासि शिवो ऽसि नः
कालकूटादिवपुषा त्राहि नः शरणागतान् ॥
1.95.m: You are fierce toward all wicked ones, you are the controller, you are benevolent to us. / By your form that swallowed the kālakūṭa poison, protect us who have sought refuge!

1.95.s:
śukraṃ tu vṛttaṃ viśveśa krīḍā vai kevalaṃ vayam
tavonmeṣanimeṣābhyām asmākaṃ pralayodayau //
1.95.d:
शुक्रं तु वृत्तं विश्वेश क्रीडा वै केवलं वयम्
तवोन्मेषनिमेषाभ्याम् अस्माकं प्रलयोदयौ ॥
1.95.m: All conduct is pure, O Lord of the universe; we are indeed merely your play. / By the opening and closing of your eyes occur our cosmic dissolution and origin.'

1.95.s:
unmīlayet tvayi brahman vināśo 'sti na te śiva
saṃtaptāsmo vayaṃ deva hariṇāmitatejasā //
1.95.d:
उन्मीलयेत् त्वयि ब्रह्मन् विनाशो ऽस्ति न ते शिव
संतप्तास्मो वयं देव हरिणामिततेजसा ॥
1.95.m: When you open your eyes, O Brahman, there is no destruction for you, O Śiva. / We are tormented, O God, by Hari of immeasurable splendor.

1.95.s:
sarvalokahitāyainaṃ tattvaṃ saṃhartumicchasi
vijñāpitas tathā devaḥ prahasanprāha tān surān //
1.95.d:
सर्वलोकहितायैनं तत्त्वं संहर्तुमिच्छसि
विज्ञापितस् तथा देवः प्रहसन्प्राह तान् सुरान् ॥
1.95.m: For the welfare of all the worlds, you wish to destroy him in reality.” / Thus addressed, the God laughed and said to those gods:

1.95.s:
abhayaṃ ca dadau teṣāṃ haniṣyāmīti taṃ prabhuḥ
so 'pi śakraḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ praṇipatya yathāgatam //
1.95.d:
अभयं च ददौ तेषां हनिष्यामीति तं प्रभुः
सो ऽपि शक्रः सुरैः सार्धं प्रणिपत्य यथागतम् ॥
1.95.m: And the Lord granted them freedom from fear, saying: “I will slay him.” / Śakra also, along with the gods, having bowed down, as they had come,

1.95.s:
jagāma bhagavān brahmā tathānye ca surottamāḥ
athotthāya mahādevaḥ śārabhaṃ rūpamāsthitaḥ //
1.95.d:
जगाम भगवान् ब्रह्मा तथान्ये च सुरोत्तमाः
अथोत्थाय महादेवः शारभं रूपमास्थितः ॥
1.95.m: The Lord Brahmā departed, and likewise the other best of gods. / Then Mahādeva, having arisen, assumed the form of a Śarabha.

1.95.s:
yayau prānte nṛsiṃhasya garvitasya mṛgāśinaḥ
apahṛtya tadā prāṇān śarabhaḥ surapūjitaḥ //
1.95.d:
ययौ प्रान्ते नृसिंहस्य गर्वितस्य मृगाशिनः
अपहृत्य तदा प्राणान् शरभः सुरपूजितः ॥
1.95.m: He went to the side of Nṛsiṃha, who was arrogant and devoured beasts. / Then, taking away his life-breaths, the Śarabha, praised by the gods,

1.95.s:
siṃhāttato naro bhūtvā jagāma ca yathākramam
evaṃ stutastadā devair jagāma sa yathākramam //
1.95.d:
सिंहात्ततो नरो भूत्वा जगाम च यथाक्रमम्
एवं स्तुतस्तदा देवैर् जगाम स यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.95.m: From a lion then became a man, and went according to due order. / Thus praised then by the gods, he departed according to due order.

1.95.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi saṃstavaṃ śārvamuttamam
rudralokamanuprāpya rudreṇa saha modate //
1.95.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि संस्तवं शार्वमुत्तमम्
रुद्रलोकमनुप्राप्य रुद्रेण सह मोदते ॥
1.95.m: Whoever recites or hears this excellent hymn to Śarva, / having reached the world of Rudra, rejoices together with Rudra.
